item.title: Icy Electronics nRF54L15 Discovery devboard integrates a snappable nRF52820 CMSIS-DAP debugger
item.description: The nRF54L15 Discovery is a compact wireless devboard with an onboard nRF52820 CMSIS-DAP debugger/programmer for Bluetooth LE, Thread, Zigbee, Matter, NFC, and other 2.4 GHz IoT applications. Its snap-apart design allows the target and interface MCUs to be used as two standalone boards. In the past, we have written about various development boards based on the Nordic nRF54L series, including the Seeed Studio XIAO nRF54L15, XIAO nRF54LM20A (Sense), and the nRF54L15 Connect Kit. The nRF54L15 Discovery board further integrates a snappable nRF52820 CMSIS-DAP debugger/programmer section. item.title: Arduino UNO Q Arcade bundle lets you build a custom retro gaming console for about $90
item.description: Arduino UNO Q Arcade bundle is a kit designed to build a custom retro gaming console. The bundle combines the Arduino UNO Q 4GB SBC with a set of daisy-chainable Modulino I2C modules, allowing users to create a custom game controller without requiring complex wiring or breadboards. The kit relies on Qwiic connectors to daisy-chain the input modules, whose data is then processed by the UNO Q to emulate standard HIDs for gaming or development. The plastic parts can be 3D printed by the user. Arduino UNO Q Arcade bundle contents: Arduino UNO Q 4GB – A Qualcomm Dragonwing QRB2210 SBC with an onboard eMMC, running Debian Linux Modulino Joystick – An I2C node configurable for simulating D-pad inputs or mouse cursor movements Modulino Buttons – An I2C node for mapping single keystrokes, multi-key shortcuts, or mouse clicks Modulino Movement – A 6-axis IMU node for motion-based mouse control Note: [...] The post Arduino UNO Q Arcade bundle lets you build a custom retro gaming console for about $90 appeared first on CNX Software - Embedded Systems News.

item.title: nRF54L Arduino Core project brings Arduino support to Nordic Semi nRF54L wireless SoCs
item.description: nRF54L Arduino Core is an open-source project designed to bring Arduino support for Nordic Semiconductor nRF54L wireless SoCs, starting with Seeed Studio’s XIAO nRF54L15 (Sense) and XIAO nRF54LM20A (Sense) boards, as well as compatible Holyiot nRF54L15 modules. Since the launch of the nRF52840-based Arduino Nano 33 BLE board in 2019, Nordic nRF52 wireless microcontrollers have been officially supported by the Arduino IDE. However, it’s not quite the case for the newer nRF54L Cortex-M33 microcontrollers. item.title: Globalscale Case8 – A MediaTek Genio 520/720 cyberdeck for gaming, home automation, and education (Crowdfunding)
item.description: Globalscale Technologies has launched the Case8 series of open-source cyberdeck-style computing platforms based on MediaTek Genio 520 and Genio 720 processors. The platform is offered in hacker (PCBA only), gaming, home automation, and education variants. The Case8 is built around an OSM-L compute module with a MediaTek Genio 520 or Genio 720 SoC with up to eight cores, a Mali-G67 GPU, and a 10 TOPS NPU. Depending on the configuration, it comes with 4GB, 8GB, or 16GB LPDDR5 memory and 64GB or 128GB UFS storage, along with Gigabit Ethernet, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.4, stereo speakers, microphones, and optional 4G/5G connectivity. Display options include a 5-inch panel for the gaming model and 7-inch touch or non-touch displays for the home automation and education variants, with camera configurations varying by model. item.title: pico-usb-wifi firmware converts the Raspberry Pi Pico W into a driverless USB WiFi adapter
item.description: pico-usb-wifi is an open-source firmware project that converts the Raspberry Pi Pico W into a driverless USB WiFi adapter that works with Windows, Linux, macOS, and other operating systems with USB CDC-NCM support. The Infineon CYW43439 chip found in the SBC can’t be used directly as a USB to WiFi bridge, and instead, the firmware implements a transparent Layer-2 bridge between the Pico W’s wireless module and USB interfaces. It basically works as an Ethernet to WiFi gateway/bridge, which exposes an Ethernet connection through USB (aka USB gadget mode) used to route Wi-Fi packets from the network. pico-usb-wifi highlights: Transparent Layer-2 Bridging between the Pico W’s wireless and USB interfaces Exposed as a USB CDC-NCM device IPv4 and IPv6 with no NAT, no private subnet, and no port-forwarding to configure Out-of-band management and debug consoles over CDC-ACM serial WPA2-PSK and WPA3-SAE authentication (and open networks) Throughput – Average 4.75 Mbits/sec; [...] The post pico-usb-wifi firmware converts the Raspberry Pi Pico W into a driverless USB WiFi adapter appeared first on CNX Software - Embedded Systems News.

item.title: Espressif Announces Aliro Solution for Interoperable Smart Access Products
item.description: Shanghai, China Espressif Systems today announced its Aliro solution, enabling developers and device makers to build interoperable smart locks and access control products using Espressif’s wireless SoCs, ESP-IDF, and Matter development ecosystem. What is Aliro Aliro, developed by the Connectivity Standards Alliance, is a new open standard for mobile access credentials. It is designed to unify digital access across smartphones, wearables, smart locks, and access readers, enabling a consistent digital key experience across residential, enterprise, hospitality, campus, and other access control scenarios. Matter and Aliro are complementary standards: Matter enables interoperable smart-home device control, while Aliro focuses on interoperable digital access credentials and unlock experiences. Aliro supports NFC for tap-to-unlock, Bluetooth LE for user-initiated access, and Bluetooth LE + UWB for secure hands-free access. Enabling Aliro for Smart Locks and Access Control Aliro addresses one of the key challenges in digital access: fragmentation across devices, access readers, credential systems, and mobile wallet ecosystems. By defining a common credential and communication framework, Aliro enables device makers to build products that can work more consistently across major mobile platforms and wallet ecosystems. Espressif’s initial Aliro solution supports Aliro NFC for tap-to-unlock applications, with Bluetooth LE and Bluetooth LE + UWB support planned for future releases. The solution can be used with Espressif’s Matter software ecosystem to build smart lock products using either Matter over Wi-Fi or Matter over Thread. Available for Developers Developers can combine Espressif Wi-Fi or Thread SoCs with an NFC module to quickly prototype and productize Aliro-enabled smart locks and access control devices. For ultra-low-power Matter over Thread products, Espressif’s next-generation SoCs--ESP32-H21 and ESP32-H4, integrate Bluetooth LE and IEEE 802.15.4 connectivity, providing a highly competitive platform for battery-powered Thread, Zigbee, Matter, and Bluetooth LE devices: ESP32-H21 features a single-core RISC-V architecture with an integrated DC-DC converter. Its streamlined architecture enables a more cost-effective solution, making it an ideal choice for access control, sensing, and other applications where both power consumption and cost are critical considerations. ESP32-H4 features a dual-core RISC-V architecture and supports external PSRAM, providing greater memory capacity and processing performance for applications with complex protocol stacks and demanding buffer requirements. Espressif has also developed a reference demo for an Aliro-enabled Matter door lock using the M5Stack NanoH2 Dev Kit, powered by ESP32-H2, and the M5Stack NFC Universal Unit based on ST25R3916. The demo showcases Matter over Thread connectivity, Aliro NFC tap-to-unlock, and integration with Espressif’s Thread SoC platform. Aliro represents an important step toward a more interoperable access control ecosystem. With Espressif’s Aliro solution, developers and device makers can build smart access products that combine digital key access, Matter ecosystem compatibility, and Espressif’s proven wireless connectivity platforms. For more information about Espressif’s Aliro solution, please refer to the blog post, or contact Espressif’s customer support team at sales@espressif.com. item.description: Germany-based Brechel Electronic has launched two new Single Pair Ethernet (SPE) expansion boards for Raspberry Pi platforms: the BE-IIS-HPP-T1S and the BE-IIS-HPP-T1L. Designed for technology evaluation, industrial network prototyping, and educational laboratory use, these boards add 10 Mbit/s Ethernet communication over a single twisted pair to standard Raspberry Pi SBCs. The BE-IIS-HPP-T1S is based on the Microchip LAN8651 10BASE-T1S MAC-PHY and supports IEEE 802.3cg Single Pair Ethernet over multidrop networks with up to 8 nodes, enabling distances up to 25 meters on a shared bus. For longer-reach point-to-point links, the company offers the BE-IIS-HPP-T1L, built around Analog Devices ADIN1110 MAC-PHY. Both boards are part of the BE-IIS HAT++ ecosystem, which allows multiple industrial communication HATs to be stacked on a single Raspberry Pi without running into SPI or GPIO resource conflicts.
